full_judgment:
8. Mr Md Asadullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioners, in course of argument has taken me through the plaint, written statement, deposition of witnesses and other materials on record and then submits that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal, inasmuch as the Court of Appeal below, without reversing findings of the trial Court, abruptly decreed the suit. He next submits that the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit on assigning sound and cogent reason that the suit land is unspecific and thus, the plaintiffs are not entitled to get relief as prayed for. 

 15. It is found that the trial Court dismissed the suit for permanent injunction on contest mainly on the ground that the plaintiffs had failed to give a clear description of the suit land. The lower Appellate Court in its turn not only failed to reverse this finding of the trial Court, also as being final Court of fact, failed to come to its own independent findings on the issues involved in this case. Therefore, I find there is a good deal of substance in the contentions of Mr Md Asadullah, the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners, that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal. 

 24. In view of the discussions made in the foregoing paragraphs, it is by now clear that the impugned judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court is not based on correct evaluation of the facts and materials of the case nor on proper appreciation of the evidence on record and, as such, the same is not a proper judgment of reversal which does not deserve to be sustained.
